senses.gloss: द्व द्व. See द्वा and द्वि.

द्वा द्वा, old nom. du. m. fr. द्व = द्वि,
two (in comp. before other numerals and before ज
and पर).
—द्वाचत्वारिंश, अस्, ई, अम्, the 42nd.
—द्वा-चत्वारिंशत्, त्, or द्वा-चत्वारिंशति, इस्, f.,
42.
—द्वा-ज, अस्, m. a son of two fathers, (formed
to explain one derivation of भर-द्वाज, which is
however more properly deduced from भरत् and
वाज.)
—द्वात्रिंश, अस्, ई, अम्, the 32nd; consist-
ing of 32.
—द्वा-त्रिंशत्, त्, f., 32.
—द्वात्रिंशद्-
अक्षरिन्, ई, m. a book or composition written in
Ślokas (consisting of 32 syllables).
—द्वात्रिंशद्-
रात्र, अम्, n., scil. सत्त्रम्, a sacrifice lasting 32
days.
—द्वात्रिंशल्-लक्षणोपेत (˚ण-उप्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, ‘having 32 auspicious marks or spots upon the
body,’ illustrious, great.
—द्वात्रिंशिका, f. occurring
in the compound भरटक-द्वात्रिंशिका, q. v.
—द्वादश, अस्, ई, अम्, the 12th (e. g. द्वादशो
भागः, the 12th part); consisting of 12, divided
into 12 parts; accompanied by or increased by 12;
(ई), f., scil. रात्रि or तिथि, the 12th day of the half
month; (अम्), n. a collection or aggregate of 12;
[cf. Gr. δώ-δεκα; Lat. duo-decim; Hib. da-deug;
Hindūst. बा-रह् through change of द् into र्; Lith.
dwy-lika through change of द् into ल्; Goth. tva-lif
through change of the guttural into the labial; Eng.
twelve; Mod. Germ. zwö-lf.]
—द्वादशक, अस्, ई,
अम्, the 12th; containing 12, consisting of 12,
amounting to 12; (अम्), n. the aggregate of 12.
—द्वादश-कपाल, अस्, ई, अम्, having 12 skulls.
—द्वादश-कर, अस्, आ, अम्, possessed of 12
hands or rays; (अस्), m. an epithet of Kārttikeya; of
Bṛhas-pati.
—द्वादश-गव, अस्, ई, अम्, having 12
oxen or cows.
—द्वादश-ता, f. or द्वादश-त्व,
अम्, n. the aggregate of 12.
—द्वादश-धा, ind.
into or in 12 parts or ways, twelvefold.
—द्वा-
दशन्, अ, m. f. n. pl., 12.
—द्वादश-पत्त्रक,
अम्, n., N. of a Yoga or particular religious observ-
ance in which the 12 syllables ॐ नमो भगवते
वासुदेवाय are connected with the 12 signs of the
zodiac and with the 12 months.
—द्वादश-भुज,
अस्, आ, अम्, having 12 arms; (अस्), m., N. of one of
Skanda's attendants.
—द्वादशम, अस्, ई, अम्, the
12th; [cf. द्वादश.]
—द्वादश-महा-वाक्य-
विवरण, अम्, n. ‘the explanation of the 12 great
words,’ N. of a philosophical work by Vaikuṇṭha-purī.
—द्वादश-मूल, अस्, m. ‘having 12 roots or
sources (?),’ an epithet of Viṣṇu.
—द्वादश-रात्र,
अम्, n. a period of 12 nights (or days); (अस्, आ, अम्),
lasting 12 nights (or days).
—द्वादशर्च (˚श-
ऋच), अस्, आ, अम्, containing 12 verses (Ṛcs).
—द्वादश-लिङ्गोद्भव (˚ग-उद्˚), अम्, n. ‘the
origin of the 12 Liṅgas,’ N. of a chapter of the
Vrata-prakāśa by Viśva-nātha.
—द्वादश-लोचन,
अस्, आ, अम्, twelve-eyed; (अस्), m. an epithet of
Kārttikeya.
—द्वादश-वार्षिक, अस्, ई, अम्, 12
years old or lasting 12 years.
—द्वादशवार्षिक-
व्रत, अम्, n. a vow for 12 years.
—द्वादश-
विध, अस्, आ, अम्, twelvefold.
—द्वादश-शत,
अम्, n., 112.
—द्वादशशत-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the
112th.
—द्वादश-साहस्र, अस्, ई, अम्, consisting
of 12000 (years).
—द्वादशांशु (˚श-अं˚), उस्, उस्,
उ, having 12 rays; (उस्), m. an epithet of Bṛhas-
pati; the planet Jupiter over which Bṛhas-pati
presides; [cf. द्वादश-कर and द्वा-दशार्चिस्.]
—द्वादशाकृति (˚श-आक्˚), इस्, इस्, इ, having 12
shapes.
—द्वादशाक्ष (˚श-अक्˚), अस्, ई, अम्, twelve-
[]
eyed; (अस्), m. an epithet of Kārttikeya; N. of
one of the attendants of Kārttikeya; a Buddha; [cf.
द्वादशाख्य.]
—द्वादशाक्षर (˚श-अक्ष्˚),
अस्, आ, अम्, containing 12 syllables; [cf. द्वादश-
पत्त्रक.]
—द्वादशाक्षर-मन्त्र, अम्, n. a
prayer of 12 syllables addressed to Viṣṇu (viz. ॐ
नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय).
—द्वादशाख्य
(˚श-आख्˚), अस्, m. a Buddha; [cf. द्वादशाक्ष.]
—द्वादशाङ्गी (˚श-अङ्˚), f. the collective sacred
writings of the Jainas (consisting of 12 parts).
—द्वा-
दशाङ्गुल (˚श-अङ्˚), अस्, m. a measure of 12
fingers.
—द्वादशात्मन् (˚श-आत्˚), आ, आ, अ, appear-
ing in 12 forms; (आ), m. or द्वादशात्मक, अस्,
m. the sun (as identified with the 12 Ādityas or the
sun in each month of the year).
—द्वादशादित्य-
तीर्थ (˚श-आद्˚), अम्, n., N. of a sacred bathing-
place.
—द्वादशादित्याश्रम (˚श-आदित्य-आश्˚), अस्,
m., N. of a sacred hermitage.
—द्वादशाध्यायी
(˚श-अध्˚), f., N. of Jaimini's Mīmāṃsā consisting
of 12 Adhyāyas.
—द्वादशान्यिक (˚श-अन्˚), अस्, आ,
अम्, one who has made 12 mistakes in reading.
—द्वादशायुस् (˚श-आय्˚), उस्, m. ‘whose life lasts
12 years,’ a dog.
—द्वादशार (˚श-अर), अस्, आ, अम्,
Ved. having 12 spokes (as the wheel or cycle of the
year).
—द्वादशारत्नि (˚श-अर्˚), इस्, इस्, इ, being
12 cubits long.
—द्वादशार्चिस् (˚श-अर्˚), इस्, इस्, इस्,
containing 12 rays; (इस्), m. an epithet of Bṛhas-
pati or the planet Jupiter; [cf. द्वादश-कर and
द्वादशांशु.]
—द्वादशाश्र or (less correctly)
द्वादशास्र, अम्, n. or द्वादशाश्रि, इस्, f. or द्वा-
दशाश्री (˚श-अश्˚), f. a dodecagon, a dodecagonal
figure.
—द्वादशाह (˚श-अह), अस्, m. a period
of 12 days; (अस्, आ, अम्), lasting 12 days; (अस्),
m. a particular ceremony lasting 12 days; [cf.
भरत-द्˚.]
—द्वादशाहिक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. द्वा-
दशन् + अहन्), relating to or coming from a
period of 12 days.
—द्वादशिक, taking place
or happening on the 12th day or on the 12th
day of a half month.
—द्वादशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, consist-
ing of 12, divided into 12.
—द्वादशी-तीर्थ, अम्,
n., N. of a sacred bathing-place mentioned in the
Śiva-Purāṇa.
—द्वादशी-व्रत, अम्, n. a peculiar
religious observance on the 12th day of a half month.
—द्वानवत, अस्, ई, अम्, the 92nd.
—द्वा-नवति,
इस्, f. = द्वि-नवति, 92.
—द्वापञ्चाश, अस्, ई, अम्,
the 52nd; accompanied by 52, increased by 52.
—द्वा-पञ्चाशत्, त्, f., 52.
—द्वापर, अस्, अम्,
m. n. that die or side of a die which is marked with
two spots or points; the Die personified; ‘the age
with the number two,’ N. of the third of the four
Yugas or ages of the world, comprising 2400 years,
(the Yuga itself = 2000, each twilight = 200 years);
the Age personified as a god; doubt, uncertainty.
—द्वाविंश, अस्, ई, अम्, the 22nd; consisting of
22.
—द्वा-विंशति, इस्, f., 22.
—द्वाविंशति-तम,
अस्, ई, अम्, the 22nd.
—द्वाविंशति-धा, in 22 parts
or ways, twenty-two-fold.
—द्वाविंशति-शत, अम्, n.,
122.
—द्वाविंशतिशत-तम, अस्, ई, अम्, the 122nd.
—द्वाषष्ट, अस्, ई, अम्, the 62nd; accompanied
by or joined with 62; [cf. द्वि-षष्टि.]
—द्वा-
षष्टि, इस्, f., 62.
—द्वाषष्टि-तम, अस्, ई, अम्,
the 62nd.
—द्वासप्तत, अस्, ई, अम्, the 72nd.
—द्वासप्तति, इस्, f., 72; [cf. द्वि-स्˚.]

द्वक, औ, du. (fem. द्वके or द्विके), Ved. two
and two, two by two.

द्वन्द द्वन्द, अम्, n. (fr. द्वन्द्व), a pair,
a couple; (अस्), m. a clock or plate on which the
hours are struck.

द्वन्द्व द्वन्द्व, अम्, n. (a reduplicated form
fr. द्व), a pair, brace, couple; a couple of animals
of different sexes, male and female; any two things
taken together, any pair of qualities or conditions
which are the opposite of one another (e. g. heat and
cold, happiness and misery, &c.); strife, contention,
bickering, dispute, quarrel, contest, fight; a fight
between two persons, a duel; doubt, uncertainty;
a stronghold, fortress; a secret; using sacrificial
vessels ?; (अस्), m. (rarely n.) a form of compound or
grammatical combination (समास) uniting two or
more words which if uncompounded would be in the
same case and connected by the conjunction ‘and,’
(this form of compound was called द्वन्द्व as
originally combining couples or pairs of things,
e. g. राम-लक्ष्मणौ, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa;
पाणि-पादम्, hand and foot); (अस्), m., N. of
several Ekāhas; the sign of the zodiac Gemini; a
species of disease, a complication of two disorders, a
compound affection of two humors [cf. निर्-द्˚];
(अम् or एन), ind. two by two.
—द्वन्द्व-चर,
अस्, आ, अम्, going about or living in couples; (अस्),
m. the ruddy goose, Anas Casarca.
—द्वन्द्व-चा-
रिन्, ई, इणी, इ, living in couples; (ई), m. the ruddy
goose.
—द्वन्द्व-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, produced or pro-
ceeding from morbid affection of two humors; pro-
ceeding from a pair &c.; arising from a quarrel,
occasioned by a dispute.
—द्वन्द्व-दुःख, अम्,
n. pain arising from alternations (as of heat and cold,
pleasure and pain, &c.).
—द्वन्द्व-भाव, अस्, m.
antagonism, discord.
—द्वन्द्व-भिन्न, अम्, n.
separation of the sexes.
—द्वन्द्व-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्,
become doubtful, hesitating, irresolute.
—द्वन्द्व-
मोह, अस्, m. trouble excited by doubt.
—द्वन्द्व-
युद्ध, अम्, n. a duel, single combat.
—द्वन्-
द्वयुद्ध-वर्णन, अम्, n. ‘description of the
single combat,’ N. of the forty-first chapter of the
Krīḍā-khaṇḍa or second part of the Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa.
—द्वन्द्व-योधिन्, ई, इनी, इ, fighting in couples
or by single combat.
—द्वन्द्व-शस्, ind. two by
two, in couples.
—द्वन्द्व-सहिष्णु-त्व, अम्, n.
ability of supporting opposites (as happiness and
misery &c.).
—द्वन्द्वातीत (˚व-अत्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
gone beyond or freed from pairs of opposite worldly
affections.
—द्वन्द्वी-भूत, अस्, आ, अम्, engaged in
single combat or close fighting.

द्वन्द्विन्, ई, इनी, इ, forming a couple; opposed to
one another; contradictory, quarrelsome, antagonistic.

द्वय द्वय, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. द्व; in Śiśupāla-b.
III. 57. द्वये nom. pl. m. occurs), twofold, double,
of two kinds or sorts; (ई), f. a pair; (अम्), n. a pair,
couple, two things, both, a brace (chiefly used at end
of comps., e. g. गो-द्वयम्, a couple of oxen); the
masc. and fem. gender (in grammar); twofold nature,
untruthfulness.
—द्वय-वादिन्, ई, इनी, इ, double-
tongued, insincere.
—द्वय-हीन, अस्, आ, अम्, desti-
tute of both (masc. and fem.) genders, i. e. neuter.
[]
—द्वयाग्नि (˚य-अग्˚), इस्, m. a kind of tree, =
पाठिन्, ह्रस्वाग्नि, commonly राञ्चिता, Plumbago
Zeylanica.
—द्वयातिग (˚य-अत्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, one
who has passed beyond or overcome the two bad
qualities, passion and ignorance, or who has sur-
mounted the several pairs of affection which disturb
the mind; (अस्), m. a saint, a holy or virtuous man.
—द्वयात्मक (˚य-आत्˚), अस्, आ, अम्, having a
twofold nature, appearing in a twofold manner.
द्वयाविन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. false, dishonest.
द्वयु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. false, dishonest; [cf. अ-द्˚.]

द्वर द्वर, अस्, आ, अम्, or द्वरि, इस्, इस्, इ, or
द्वरिन्, ई, इणी, इ (fr. rt. द्वृ), Ved. obstructing.

द्वार, अम्, n. a door, gate, gateway, passage,
entrance, opening (cf. वक्त्र-द्वार and सहस्र-
द्˚; the body is sometimes called नव-द्वारम्
पुरम्, a city with nine gates or openings); a
way, means, medium, vehicle, (the Māheśvaras hold
that there are six Dvāras or means of obtaining
a wished-for object); (एण), ind. by means of,
by; with regard to, according to; (ई), f. a door;
[cf. अ-द्˚.]
—द्वार-कण्टक, अस्, m. ‘door-
thorn,’ the bolt of a door; a door, gate.
—द्वा-
र-कपाट, अस् or अम्, m. or n. (?), the leaf or
fold of a door, the panel of a door.
—द्वार-ता,
f. a gate, door, an entrance, way, access.
—द्वार-
दर्शिन्, ई, m. ‘watching the door,’ a door-keeper.
—द्वार-दातु (?), उस्, m. a species of tree, = वर-
दातु, भूमि-सह.
—द्वार-दारु, उस्, m. (?), ‘hav-
ing wood fit for a door,’ the tree Tectona Grandis,
teak.
—द्वार-नायक, अस्, m. or द्वार-प, अस्, m.
a door-keeper, porter, warder.
—द्वार-पट्ट, अस्,
m. the panel or surface of a door; the curtain of a
door.
—द्वार-पति, इस्, m. a door-keeper, warder;
N. of a kingdom (?).
—द्वार-पाल, अस्, m. a door-
keeper, warder; an epithet of various Yakṣas and
of sacred places connected with them.
—द्वार-पा-
लक, अस्, m. a door-keeper; (इका), f. a metronymic
from Dvāra-pālī.
—द्वार-पिण्डी, f. the threshold of
a door.
—द्वार-पिधान or द्वारापिधान (˚र-
अप्˚), अस्, m. the bolt of a door.
—द्वार-बलि-भुज्, क्,
m. ‘eating the offering (of food) scattered before the
door,’ the bird Ardea Nivea; a crow; a sparrow.
—द्वार-बाहु, उस्, m. ‘door-arm,’ a door-post, jamb.
—द्वार-महिम-वर्णन, अम्, n. ‘description
of the glory of the dvāra,’ N. of the 127th chapter
of the Krīḍā-khaṇḍa or second part of the Gaṇeśa-
Purāṇa.
—द्वार-यन्त्र, अम्, n. ‘door-implement
or door-restrainer,’ a lock, bolt.
—द्वार-वत्, आन्,
अती, अत्, having many doors; (अती), f., N. of the
capital of Kṛṣṇa; [cf. द्वारका and द्वार्-वती.]
—द्वारवती-निर्माण, अम्, n. ‘the construction of
Dvāra-vatī,’ N. of the 116th Adhyāya of the Vārāha-
Purāṇa.
—द्वार-वर्त्मन्, अ, n. a gateway.
—द्वा-
र-वृत्त, अम्, n. black pepper.
—द्वार-शाखा, f.
the leaf of a door, division of a door.
—द्वार-स्तम्-
भ, अस्, m. a door-post.
—द्वार-स्थ, अस्, आ, अम्,
standing at the door; (अस्), m. a door-keeper, porter.
—द्वाराधिप or द्वाराध्यक्ष (˚र-अध्˚), अस्,
m. ‘superintendent of the door,’ a door-keeper, porter,
warder, chamberlain.
—द्वाराभिमानिन् (˚र-अभ्˚),
ई, इनी, इ, assuming the character of the (sacrificial)
doors.
—द्वारा-वती, f. = द्वार-वती, q. v.

द्वार् द्वार्, र्, f. (said to be fr. rt. द्वृ),
Ved. a gate, door, entrance; access, way; expedient,
means, opportunity; द्वारा, inst. c., at the end of a
comp. = by means of, by; [cf. 1. दुर्, 2. दुर; Zend
dvara-m, ‘gate, palace;’ Gr. θύρα, θύρ-ε-τρο-ν,
θύρασι, θυρί-ς, θυρ-εό-ς, θαιρό-ς; Lat. for-ē-s, foris,
foras; Umbr. vero, ‘gate,’ for dvero; perhaps also
πύλη and porta, d being dropped and v changed
into p, as in Zend aspa = ἵππος from Sanskrit अश्व;
Goth. daur; Angl. Sax. duru, dyr; Old Germ.
tor; Slav. dverĭ, ‘gate, door;’ Lith. dùr-ys, ‘door;’
Hib. dor, doras, ‘a door, gate.’]
—द्वाः-स्थ or
द्वा-स्थ or द्वाः-स्थित or द्वा-स्थित, अस्, आ, अम्,
standing at the gate or door; (अस्), m. a door-keeper,
porter, warder.
—द्वार्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, having many
doors; (अती), f. = द्वार-वती, q. v.

द्वारक = द्वार above; (आ or इका), f. ‘the city
with many gates,’ N. of the capital of Kṛṣṇa (on
the western point of Guzerāt, supposed to have been
submerged by the sea).
—द्वारका-दास, अस्, m.
‘slave of Dvārakā,’ N. of a man.
—द्वारका-प्र-
वेश, अस्, m. ‘the entrance into Dvārakā,’ N. of the
103rd chapter of the Kṛṣṇa-khaṇḍa or fourth part
of the Brahma-vaivarta-Purāṇa.
—द्वारका-माहात्-
म्य, अम्, n. ‘the glory of Dvārakā,’ N. of a part
of the Skanda-Purāṇa.
—द्वारकारम्भ (˚का-आर्˚),
अस्, m. ‘the commencement of Dvārakā,’ N. of the
102nd chapter of the Kṛṣṇa-khaṇḍa of the Brahma-
vaivarta-Purāṇa.
—द्वारकेश (˚का-ईश), अस्, m. ‘the
lord of Dvārakā,’ an epithet of Kṛṣṇa.

द्वारिक, अस्, m. a door-keeper, warder; N. of
one of the eighteen attendants of the Sun; (इका), f.,
see द्वारक.
द्वारिन्, ई, m. a door-keeper, porter, warder.

द्वार्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to a door, being at
a door; (आ), f., scil. स्थूणा, a door-post.
